Deconvolution Identifiability Plot Type

Source: R/type_identifiability.R
type_identifiability.Rd

Creates publication-ready deconvolution identifiability plots that explain why specific cell types are detected versus zeroed in bulk tissue deconvolution. Combines marker gene counts (bars) on the primary axis with pairwise collinearity metrics (triangles) on a secondary axis.

Usage

type_identifiability(
  collinearity = NULL,
  status = NULL,
  flag = NULL,
  max_marker_scale = NULL,
  bar_width = 0.62,
  point_size = 2.8,
  status_colors = c(predicted = "#2E8B57", zeroed = "#C0C0C0"),
  flag_colors = c(identifiable = "#2166AC", collinear = "#B2182B", `few markers` =
    "#F4A582", `few markers + collinear` = "#7B3294"),
  ...
)

Arguments

collinearity

Column name or vector for maximum collinearity correlation (Pearson r in [0, 1]). Default looks for "max_corr".

status

Column name or vector for deconvolution status (e.g. "predicted" vs "zeroed"). Default looks for "status".

flag

Column name or vector for identifiability diagnostic flag (e.g. "identifiable", "collinear", "few markers", "few markers + collinear"). Default looks for "note" or "flag".

max_marker_scale

Numeric scaling factor for secondary axis transformation (default auto-detected from maximum marker count).

bar_width

Numeric bar width (default 0.62).

point_size

Numeric point size for collinearity glyphs (default 2.8).

status_colors

Named vector of fill colors for deconvolution status (default: predicted = "#2E8B57", zeroed = "#C0C0C0").

flag_colors

Named vector of colors for identifiability diagnostic flags (default: identifiable = "#2166AC", collinear = "#B2182B", few markers = "#F4A582", few markers + collinear = "#7B3294").

...

Additional arguments.

Value

A cliplot_type object for use with cliplot.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df_ident = data.frame(
  cell_type = c("T_cell", "B_cell", "Macrophage", "Keratinocyte"),
  n_markers = c(13, 3, 42, 32),
  max_corr  = c(0.57, 0.90, 0.77, 0.46),
  status    = c("predicted", "predicted", "predicted", "zeroed"),
  note      = c("identifiable", "few markers + collinear", "collinear", "identifiable")
)
cliplot(n_markers ~ cell_type, data = df_ident, type = type_identifiability())
} # }
